info.title: agency
info.description:
agency: Agents at your command, across all your computers. People, their Claude Code and agents themselves use this API to start agents on your computers, talk to them and follow what they do. It runs lasting Claude Code **agents** on a fleet of hosts. Each agent lives on one host and runs in **sessions**; a **role** says what it starts with.

- **Create** an agent on a host, or **request** one in a role, started once Claude usage and a host's room allow. Admission starts the highest role `priority` first, then the oldest.
- **Talk to it** with `SendMessage`, which starts a session carrying on its conversation when none is live; `StopAgent` ends its session and keeps it, for a message to start it again; `DeleteAgent` ends it for good. Its session also ends when it says it is done and its role says so.
- **Follow it**: its `status` is `working`, `idle`, `waiting` (on the person), `review` or `done`, which it says of itself with `PutAgentStatus`; `ListTranscriptLines` reads what it said, after a cursor.
- **Hosts** run agency-host, which keeps a WebSocket open at `/socket`: heartbeats and reports go up it, commands come down it (`SocketInbound`, `SocketOutbound`). You don't call it. A page watches live with a ticket from `CreateSocketTicket`.

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with the stage's token, on everything but `GetHealth`, the page and the docs.

**Roles** are honed skills, `agent-roles/<name>`, read here and changed in honed.

**Errors:** `{code, message}`, where `code` is an AWS-style exception name such as `ValidationException` or `ResourceNotFoundException`.

agents.description: Agents on the host and what each is doing. One not named is unchanged.

lines.description: Transcript lines not yet sent on a socket that took them.

commandResults.description: One per command taken since it was last reported. A reported command is delivered, and is neither pushed again nor replayed to a socket that connects.

tokens.description: Running token totals of sessions whose count has grown since it was last reported.

SocketReport.description: Host to service, the only way a host reports: whenever something changes, and in full (every agent, every line and result not yet sent) whenever its socket connects. Pushed on to viewers. Idempotent: lines by (`agentId`, `seq`), results by `commandId`. Does not count as a heartbeat. A socket message is at most 128 KB, sent in frames of 32 KB at most, so lines that would not fit go in the reports after it.

id.description: Assigned by the service when the agent is created.

state.description: `idle`: no session running. `working`: its session is taking a turn (from Claude Code's `system` `init` to its `result`). `waiting`: its session is running and between turns. `interrupted`: a session the service started is not running, and was not stopped (a crash, a restart, or a session it does not know).

sessionId.description: The session running, or null for none.

tasks.description: Background tasks and subagents its session has open, as Claude Code's latest `background_tasks_changed` lists them, whether or not a turn is running; 0 once its session ends. Absent from a host that does not say, read as 0.

told.description: Whether the turn running, or the last one, began with a message the host delivered (its echo came back in that turn), rather than by itself, as a turn a background task's end begins does. Absent from a host that does not say, read as unknown.

agentId.description: Assigned by the service when the agent is created.

sessionId.description: Assigned by the service when it queues the session's `start`.

seq.description: Deduplicated by (`agentId`, `seq`), so resending is safe.

from.description: `instruction`: a message sent to the agent.

text.description: Kept whole up to 65536 characters, and past that cut rather than refused, so the rest of its report is not lost with it. A text cut short, by its host to fit a socket message or here, ends `… [cut: N of M characters]`: N kept of the M there were.

commandId.description: On an `instruction` line that is a command's text as the session took it (a `message`, a `start`'s first message, an `interrupt`'s text): that command's id. Absent on any other line.
The command reported on, by its `id`.

ok.description: False when the host could not do the command.

error.description: Why not, when `ok` is false, in the host's words.

SessionTokensReport.description: A session's running total of tokens so far, not what was used since the last report. The service keeps the highest of each count reported for the session, so a total sent again, or late, never adds twice.

readAt.description: When the session's stream said it: its `rate_limit_event`'s time.

allOf.description: The weekly window; absent when the event did not carry it.

UsageReport.description: The account's usage, when a session's stream has said it since the last report.

utilization.description: How much of the window's allowance is used, 0 to 1 (1 is all of it).

resetsAt.description: When the window starts again from 0.

UsageWindowReport.description: The 5-hour window; absent when the event did not carry it.

version.description: The agency-host build that sent the heartbeat.

labels.description: What the host offers, as its owner configured it. A full snapshot; absent, the host's last labels stand (none for a new host).

capacity.description: How many sessions the host will run at once. Absent, capacity is unknown.

Heartbeat.description: Up a host's socket, after its first full report on connecting and then every 30 seconds: that it is there and what it offers. The first from a host id registers it, and only these keep a host `connected`.

SocketPing.description: Either side's keep-alive, beside the server's WebSocket pings, which close a socket that misses one.

CommandPush.description: To every socket of the command's host, the moment it is queued; and to a host's socket once it is open, every command still pending for that host, oldest first. That replay follows the first message the host sends on it (its full report on connecting), and leaves out commands that message reports. A command is pending until a report names it, or until it is withdrawn; a host may see one more than once, and knows it by `id`.

env.description: Set in the session's environment: the addresses of the services it is given. Never a secret.

secrets.description: The tokens of `credentials`, by variable, read as the command is pushed to the host's socket and never stored, so a listed or replayed command holds none and a rotated secret reaches the next start. The host writes them to a file in the agent's folder that only it can read, and the session's environment is set from that file, never from a command line.

mcpServers.description: The MCP servers the session may call, by service, as Claude Code's `mcpServers` takes them: each given service that serves one, its address and token written as `${URL_VAR}` and `${TOKEN_VAR}`, which the session's own environment fills, so the command holds no token, and an `x-actor` header with the agent's name, so a service that records who wrote what names the agent. The host passes them to Claude Code with `--mcp-config`.

id.description: Assigned by the service when the agent is created.

name.description: Unique among agents not deleted. Names its home folder and tmux session on its host.

title.description: What the agent named itself for its work, with `PutAgentTitle`, or the person with `UpdateAgent`. Kept across sessions; null until one is given. Unlike `name`, it names nothing on its host.

label.description: A short tag given when it was made or with `UpdateAgent`, shown beside its name. Null for none.

item.description: The work item it was started on, as given when it was made; null for none.

role.description: The role it was made from, as given when it was made; null for one made without.

createdBy.description: The `claimed-by` header of the `CreateAgent` call that made it, unverified. Null when it had none.

whenDone.description: What becomes of the agent once it says it is `done`: `keep`, it stays and a message starts it again; `stop`, its session is stopped; `delete`, it is stopped and deleted, as by `DeleteAgent`. On `review`, `stop` and `delete` both only stop its session, so a send-back can still start it again. Whatever it is, an agent `done` with no session for longer than agency's `--retire-closed-after` days (14 unless set) is deleted by its hourly sweep.

skills.description: The honed skills each session is given, by name: its role's own first.

credentials.description: The services each session is given, by name; null for every one the stage has. Never a token.

state.description: `idle`: has a home and no live session. `working`, `waiting`: a live session, in a turn or between turns, as its host last reported it (`working` too from the moment a `start` or a message is queued). `interrupted`: its session ended without a stop, and it can be resumed. `deleted`: no longer on the team; its home folder is kept on the host.

id.description: Assigned by the service when it queues the session's `start`.

skills.description: The honed skills it started with, in order.

contextNote.description: Why a skill it was made with was left out, or given from honed's last good copy; null when none was.

session.description: The live session, or null for none: when it started, and what it started with.

reportedAt.description: When its host last reported a change to it; null until its host first reports it.

status.description: What it is doing, as its host sees its turns and as it last said. `working`: a turn of its, or a background task or subagent it started, is running. `idle`: its session is live and neither is, as after it replied; this never needs the person. `waiting`: it said with `PutAgentStatus` that it needs the person, and stays so until the person messages it (a turn it begins by itself does not end it). `review`: its change is submitted to approval-service, said by the agent or by approval-service, and it waits on the reviewer until the change ships or is sent back. `done`: it finished what it was made for, or its change shipped. `review` and `done` are kept once its session ends, and no turn changes them; only a message from the person, or `PutAgentStatus`, does. Otherwise null without a live session. Only `waiting` should notify the person.

summary.description: One line it, or approval-service, last said with `PutAgentStatus`: what it is doing, while `waiting` what it needs from the person. Cleared by a message from the person.

headline.description: A few words said with its `summary` and gone with it, for a list of agents. Null when none was given.

saidAt.description: When `summary` was said; null when there is none.

activity.description: What its latest transcript line says it was doing, and when: a Bash call's description (never its command), another tool's name and target (`Edit src/fleet.ts`, `Agent <its description>`), or the first line of a reply. Never what the person said. Show whichever of it and `summary` is newer, by `at` and `saidAt`. Null until it has done something.

tasks.description: Background tasks and subagents its live session has open, as its host last reported; 0 without one.

told.description: Whether its live session's current or last turn began with a message delivered to it (the person's, or a brief), rather than by itself, as a turn a background task's end begins does; so `idle` after a turn that was told is a reply. Null without a live session, or when its host has not said.

hostStatus.description: Its host's `status`. While the host is `disconnected` or `lost`, `state` may be out of date.

inputTokens.description: Input tokens not read from or written to the prompt cache.

cacheReadInputTokens.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache.

Tokens.description: Tokens its sessions have used, summed, as its host reported each session's running total; every count 0 until one is reported. A live session's count still grows.

queuedAt.description: When it was queued for its host.

delivery.description: `queued`: not yet reported by the host. `withdrawn`: never to be sent, because it went unreported for 300 seconds (`create` and `delete` excepted). `done` / `rejected`: the host reported it, done (a text: delivered to the session) or not.

labels.description: As the host last declared them.

available.description: How many more sessions it will take now: `capacity` minus its agents with a live session. Null when `capacity` is.

post.description: Records the request `waiting`, then admits what it can at once. A request starts once both usage windows read under 90% (from a reading under 15 minutes old, or one whose window has since reset) and a connected host carrying its `labels` has a free slot; of those waiting, the highest role `priority` first, then the oldest. Admission runs when a request is made and on every host's heartbeat, every 30 seconds while any host is connected, which is when a host's capacity and usage are next known. A reading older than that, of a window not since reset, still admits one request at a time while both windows read under 70%: one starts once none has since that reading, or none in the last 15 minutes, so the agent it starts gives the next reading. Admitted, the agent is made from its role as `CreateAgent` with `role` would, with this request's id as its own and a name of the service's choosing (`<role>-<first 8 of its id>`), placed on a host of the service's choosing; `agentId` names it. A request names no host or agent name.

delete.description: Records it `deleted` at once, ends any session, frees its name, and queues a `stop` if it had a live session and then `delete`, which is offered until its host takes it. agency keeps its record, sessions and transcript. put.description: Called by the agent itself, from its `page` skill, and by approval-service for the agent whose change it took or shipped. `waiting` says the agent needs the person; it stands until the person messages it. `working` only says what it is doing: whether it reads `working` or `idle` is its host's turns. `review` says its change is submitted to approval-service and `done` that it finished, or its change shipped; each needs no live session. Not sent to its host. Once the agent is in `review` or `done` and no turn or background task of its runs, `whenDone` is carried out: `stop` stops its session, and `delete` deletes it once `done` (in `review` it is stopped, never deleted, so a send-back reaches it).
